model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2025 net rental income, proportionally consolidated (FY25 AR Table: NRI total 180.2; HMSO.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:1550). NRI is the REIT's revenue line for this model; gross rental income and service-charge pass-throughs are excluded.
inputs.share_count_basis: 585,217,753 shares in issue after the July/Aug 2026 Manchester Arndale placing (~10% primary placing + RetailBook offer at 355p; Analysis.json recent_developments; corroborated by FY25 shares in issue 532.1m x 1.10 = 585.3m) plus 2.1m potentially dilutive share awards (FY25 AR note 10A, HMSO.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:9058). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it. The two 10% placings (Aug-25, Aug-26) were acquisition funding, not compensation, and are already in the 585.2m count; the flows include the acquired assets' NRI. A further placing for a further acquisition would be modelled when announced.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net debt is deliberately held at ZERO in the engine. The capitalised stream (EPRA earnings) is already after net finance costs (FY25 GBP39.2m; FY26 guided c.GBP60m), so it is an equity flow discounted at the cost of equity; deducting net debt again would charge the debt twice. Actual net debt for the reader: GBP1,369.8m at 31 Dec 2025 (FY25 AR), c.GBP1.4bn at 30 Jun 2026 (H1 FY26 presentation p.18), pro forma c.GBP1.37bn / LTV c.36% / net debt:EBITDA c.7x after the Dublin Central disposal, Arndale acquisition and placing.
inputs.last_fcf_definition: FY2025 AFFO proxy = EPRA earnings 104.3 less total capital expenditure 33.6 (cash flow statement). This is the equity-level distributable cash flow the model capitalises; NOT OCF-less-capex.
inputs.reported_fcf_definition: FY2025 operating cash flow 96.9 less capex 33.6 (Metrics.csv). Shown for audit only; OCF for an IAS 40 REIT includes working-capital noise and is not the valuation base.
inputs.sbc_source: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2025 = 4.5 (cash-flow share-based payments add-back printed as 3.9 at HMSO.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:9974; CSV figure includes associated employer costs). EquityAwardTaxes 0 in every year. SBC is already a cost inside EPRA earnings; the engine's EBITDA margin is anchored to (EPRA earnings + SBC + tax)/NRI so that SBC is charged exactly once via sbc_pct_path.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY25 finance income GBP33.4m is inside net finance costs and therefore inside EPRA earnings. It is NOT stripped because no cash is added back in the bridge (net debt held at zero): the matching-asset rule is satisfied on both sides.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 share buyback and cancellation GBP25.7m (balance of the up-to-GBP140m programme funded by the 2024 Value Retail exit). Programme is complete; the company is now an issuer (two ~10% placings in 12 months), so the flat count is a modelling convention, not a funded one.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quoted pence. No cross-currency FX involved; no dual listing parity check needed (JSE secondary listing in ZAR exists but is not the quote used here).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T15:35:19Z regular London close (Yahoo Finance chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a GBP COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the capitalised flow is post-interest. Build: UK 10y gilt c.4.6% (Oct 2026 range 4.4-4.8%; Yahoo has no gilt series, so this is a stated assumption) + 5.0% UK ERP x equity beta c.1.0 for a geared pure-play retail REIT = 9.6%, rounded to 9.5%. Cross-check: at 326p the shares yield c.6% on FY26 DPS (80-85% of c.22.5p run-rate EPRA EPS) with 4-5% LfL growth guided, implying a market CoE of c.9-10%. The same 9.5% is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once, through the weights and the driver paths).
inputs.lease_treatment: Hammerson is the lessor; head-lease liabilities (GBP1-7m) are immaterial and are inside net finance costs. No separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: EPRA earnings are attributable (NCI GBP0.4m deducted, FY25 AR line 1544). No further NCI deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run on the Drivers/engine route with net debt held at zero (same construction as GPT.AX, GMG.AX, CHC.AX). Chosen because Hammerson is an IAS 40 fair-value REIT: reported net income is revaluation noise (FY19-FY24 losses of GBP0.05-1.7bn/yr; FY25 profit 232m includes GBP120m revaluation gains), OCF-less-capex is distorted by JV distributions and working capital, and 'net debt' at 8x EBITDA would make an owner-FCF DCF meaningless. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = proportionally consolidated NRI; ebitda_margin = (EPRA earnings + SBC + tax)/NRI, i.e. the stream is already after admin costs and net finance costs (FY25 anchor: (104.3+4.5+0.7)/180.2 = 60.8%; FY26 guidance implies (132+4.8+1.0)/230.7 = 59.7%); sbc_pct charges SBC once; da_pct = 0 (investment property is not depreciated); cash_tax_rate 1% (UK REIT / French SIIC regimes; FY25 cash tax GBP1.1m); capex_pct = MAINTENANCE capex only (FY26 guide GBP30-40m asset enhancement and leasing on NRI c.231m = 13-17%; FY25 actual total capex 33.6m = 18.6% of NRI). The c.GBP30m repositioning/stewardship completion and GBP10-15m development spend are growth capex funding the strategic-land pipeline and are excluded from the flows; the corresponding land is added in equity_bridge at a 50% haircut so neither the cost nor the asset is counted twice. wc_capture 0 (no deferred-revenue model). FY26 YEAR-1 CHECK: 230.7 NRI x 59.7% - SBC 4.8 - tax 1.3 - capex 34.6 = c.GBP97m AFFO = 16.5p/share on 587.3m shares, versus guided EPRA earnings GBP132m (22.5p run-rate on the post-placing count; reported FY26 EPRA EPS will print higher, c.24p, because the placing shares were only in issue for H2). PRICE: regular close, not after-hours; the price is in pence and the model's unsuffixed per-share values are in pence via fx_rate 100.
inputs.guidance_anchor: H1 FY26 results 30 Jul 2026: FY26 EPRA earnings c.GBP132m (c.GBP125m underlying + GBP7m H2 Arndale), total NRI growth c.28%, LfL NRI growth 4-5%, EPRA cost ratio <30% in FY26 and -300-400bps again in FY27, net finance costs c.GBP60m, capex GBP30-40m asset enhancement/leasing + c.GBP30m repositioning + GBP10-15m development, dividend 80-85% of EPRA earnings. Medium term off the FY25 base: 6-8% EPRA EPS CAGR, 6-8% DPS CAGR, c.10% total accounting return.
inputs.nta_cross_check: EPRA NTA 394p at 31 Dec 2025 and 30 Jun 2026 (unchanged); c.390p pro forma after the 355p placing (c.1% dilutive). Price 326p = 17% discount to NTA. The AFFO model values the income stream, not the appraisal; a base value below NTA says the market-implied cap rate on the equity stream (9.5% CoE less 2.5% growth) is wider than the valuers' property yields (portfolio topped-up NIY c.7-7.8%) after leverage and overheads, which is normal for a geared UK retail REIT.

balance_sheet_memo.note: Memo only; the engine holds net debt at zero because the capitalised stream is post-interest. Pro forma figures per H1 FY26 presentation p.12/p.18 footnotes (post Dublin Central disposal, Arndale acquisition, placing).

equity_bridge.item: Strategic land at 50% of book value
equity_bridge.note: GBP291m pro forma book value of strategic land (Edgbaston Gardens, The Drum, Cabot Gate PBSA, Martineau Galleries, The Goodsyard, Oracle land; H1 FY26 presentation / Analysis.json). It produces c.GBP5m of 'developments and other' NRI, i.e. essentially nothing in the capitalised stream, so under the matching-asset rule it is added back. Haircut 50% because realisation requires development capex that is excluded from the flows, planning and multi-year execution, and because disposals of such land have historically completed at or below book. The debt that funds it is already serviced inside net finance costs. Worth c.25p/share.

historical_growth.revenue_note: NRI proportionally consolidated: FY2020 157.6 -> FY2022 177.2 -> FY2025 180.2. Flat headline because disposals (VIA Outlets 2020, Value Retail 2024, non-core UK/Irish/French assets) offset LfL growth and the FY25 JV buy-outs.
historical_growth.eps_note: EPRA EPS 13.0p (FY20, post rights issue) -> 21.2p (FY22) -> 20.7p (FY25). The 5yr figure is recovery from the pandemic trough; the 3yr figure is flat because the Value Retail exit (GBP19m of FY24 EPRA earnings) was replaced by JV buy-outs only in H2 FY25.
historical_growth.equity_note: Shareholders' equity 3,208.8 (FY20) -> 2,586.4 (FY22) -> 2,094.8 (FY25); NTA/share 820p -> 526p -> 394p. Driven by revaluation losses through FY24 and the Value Retail write-down; FY25 NTA +6%. Not a forward growth proxy.
historical_growth.fcf_note: AFFO proxy (EPRA earnings less total capex): FY2022 68.5 -> FY2025 70.7 (1.1% CAGR). FY2020/21 AFFO was negative (EPRA earnings 36.5/65.5 vs capex 68.1/76.9), so no 5yr CAGR is defined. Reported OCF-less-capex went from -150.5 (FY20) to 63.3 (FY25) and is not a meaningful series for a fair-value REIT.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Forward: FY26 guided LfL NRI growth 4-5% and the new medium-term 6-8% EPRA EPS CAGR off the FY25 base, haircut to the LfL rate for the years after the acquisitions annualise. Historical CAGRs are all dominated by disposals and revaluations and are not used.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity/NTA CAGR is deeply negative (-8%/yr) while EPRA EPS compounded +10%/yr over 5 years: the divergence is the pandemic-era revaluation and deleveraging cycle (rights issue, VIA Outlets and Value Retail exits), not a signal about the forward income stream. Flagged; growth selection taken from guidance instead.

base.growth_note: FY26 +28% = guidance (Bullring/Brent Cross/Oracle buy-outs annualising + H2 Arndale). FY27 +8% = full-year Arndale (c.GBP15-17m vs GBP7m in FY26) + 4.5% LfL. Then LfL only, decelerating from the guided 4-5% to 2.5% as reversionary leasing spreads normalise. No further acquisitions assumed (they would come with their own placings).
base.ebitda_margin_note: Margin = (EPRA earnings + SBC + tax)/NRI. FY25 actual 60.8%; FY26 59.7% ties to guided EPRA earnings GBP132m with net finance costs c.GBP60m (up from 39m on the debt-funded buy-outs). FY27-28 recover 80-180bps as the EPRA cost ratio falls another 300-400bps and the Arndale income arrives equity-funded; capped at 61.5% because the 2027 bond refinancing (EUR700m 1.75% replaced by 3.5%/3.875% paper) absorbs the rest of the cost-ratio gain.
base.capex_note: Maintenance capex (asset enhancement and leasing incentives) only: FY26 guide GBP30-40m on NRI 231m = 15%; drifts to 13% as the repositioning programme completes and the NRI base grows. Repositioning and development spend excluded (growth capex; land in equity_bridge).

bull.growth_note: Top of the guided 6-8% EPS CAGR: LfL NRI at 5-6% as four years of double-digit leasing spreads keep converting into passing rent, Arndale re-letting and Cergy 3 add on top, and the polarisation tailwind persists.
bull.ebitda_margin_note: Cost ratio falls to the mid-20s and deleveraging toward the 6-8x guiderail trims finance costs as a share of a growing NRI base.

bear.growth_note: FY26 slightly short of guidance; FY27 Arndale annualises but LfL fades; FY28-30 flat NRI as a UK consumer downturn brings occupier failures and negative reversion at renewal; modest recovery thereafter.
bear.ebitda_margin_note: Finance costs rise as the 2027 maturities and RCFs refinance at today's coupons with no offsetting deleveraging, vacancy costs lift the cost ratio back above 30%, and the equity stream absorbs it all because the debt is fixed.
bear.capex_note: Defensive capex rises: re-letting failed anchor space and MEES (EPC C by April 2027) compliance on a flat NRI base.

scenario_narratives.base: Hammerson delivers FY26 guidance (EPRA earnings c.GBP132m, NRI +28%) as the Bullring, Brent Cross and Oracle buy-outs annualise and Manchester Arndale contributes from H2. FY27 carries the full-year Arndale uplift; thereafter growth is like-for-like only, decelerating from the guided 4-5% to 2.5% as the reversionary gap closes. The EPRA cost ratio keeps falling but the 2027 refinancing of cheap 2017-vintage euro bonds absorbs much of that gain, so the post-interest margin plateaus around 61.5% of NRI. Maintenance capex of 13-15% of NRI is deducted; strategic land is credited at half of book. Capitalised at a 9.5% GBP cost of equity with 2.5% terminal growth. No further acquisitions or placings assumed.
scenario_narratives.bull: The polarisation thesis holds: flagship footfall and sales keep beating national benchmarks, leasing spreads stay double-digit, and LfL NRI runs at 5-6% for several years while Arndale re-letting and Cergy 3 add on top, landing at the top of the 6-8% EPS CAGR guidance. The cost ratio reaches the mid-20s, deleveraging toward the 6-8x guiderail trims finance costs, and the equity margin widens to 63%. Terminal growth 3%. This is the scenario in which the 17% discount to NTA closes.
scenario_narratives.bear: A UK consumer downturn and 'higher for longer' rates arrive together: occupier failures and negative reversion flatten NRI from FY28, vacancy costs push the cost ratio back above 30%, and the 2027 bond and RCF maturities refinance at today's coupons with no offsetting deleveraging, so the post-interest margin compresses to 55%. Defensive and MEES capex rises to 17% of NRI. Leverage already sits above the company's own guiderails (8.1x annualised, LTV 39%), so there is no balance-sheet cushion and a further dilutive placing becomes likely; this is the re-leveraging-into-a-downturn pattern that forced the 2020 rights issue.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25% because leverage is above management's own guiderails (net debt:EBITDA 8.1x vs 6-8x, LTV 39% vs c.35%), GBP609m of 2027 maturities plus the RCFs need refinancing, and growth has been funded by two ~10% placings in twelve months; the FY25 Viability Statement itself says 'significant refinancing is required'. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (LfL growth sustained at 5%+, cost ratio to the mid-20s, deleveraging without further dilution). Base 50%: management has met or raised guidance in each of the last three reporting periods.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Capitalise the equity income stream a shareholder actually receives (EPRA earnings less maintenance capex, already after interest), at a GBP cost of equity, and credit the non-income-producing strategic land separately at a haircut. Do not deduct debt again, do not treat revaluation gains as earnings, and do not use NTA as the value: NTA is an appraisal cross-check, and for a geared retail REIT the income-based value sits below it whenever the equity cap rate (CoE less growth) is wider than the property yield after overheads and leverage. The 15% hurdle entry price is far below intrinsic value, as it must be for an asset discounted at 9.5%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: each 100bps on the 9.5% CoE moves base value by roughly 12-15%; the sensitivity grid covers 7.5-11.5%.

Maintenance capex definition: deducting the full GBP70-85m FY26 capex (including repositioning and development) instead of the GBP30-40m asset-enhancement line would cut value by c.100p/share; crediting none of it would add c.60p. The split is a judgment anchored to management's own guidance categories.

Refinancing of the 2027 euro bonds and RCFs: the base assumes the margin plateau already absorbs the coupon step-up; a wider credit spread or a rating reversal would push the margin toward the bear path.
Further acquisitions funded by placings below NTA (355p vs 394p) are accretive to EPS but dilutive to NTA; the model does not assume any, in either direction.
Strategic land credited at 50% of GBP291m book (c.25p/share); realisation depends on planning and development execution outside the flows.

Price is in pence against GBP millions in the statements; fx_rate 100 is a unit conversion, not a currency exposure. Euro-denominated income and bonds create a modest GBP/EUR translation exposure that flows through NTA, not the model.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular London close, GBp); 52-week range 280.4-391.8.
data_sources.financials: HMSO.L_Metrics.csv (annual FY2017-FY2025, interims through H1 FY2026, GBP millions) derived from core_metrics; FY25 AR (HMSO.L_Annual_FY2025.txt) EPRA earnings analysis lines 1536-1550, share count note 10A lines 9053-9065, cash flow and share-based payments line 9974; H1 FY26 results presentation (HMSO.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt) pp.12-19 for net debt, NTA, pro forma leverage and FY26 guidance.
data_sources.qualitative: HMSO.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): business model, Manchester Arndale acquisition and placing terms (585,217,753 shares), medium-term guidance, bull/bear cases, risk register.
